data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.cost_note: cost_mentions_in_text are sentences from the NASA catalog description that state a dollar amount (planned, estimated or total); the scope and year are whatever the sentence says.
record.name: Kepler
record.description: Description Kepler was an American (NASA) astronomy probe launched by a Delta 2 rocket from Cape Canaveral at 03:50 UT on 07 March 2009. Kepler's mission was to search for Earth-sized planets around other stars by looking for brightness variations in over 100,000 stars in the Cygnus-Lyra region. The photometer on Kepler continuously monitored the same star-field in a 12-degree field of view over the nominal 3.5 year lifetime, allowing multiple observations of transits of exoplanets in orbits up to one year. In order to maintain a stable pointing attitude, the spacecraft was placed into a Earth-trailing heliocentric orbit of period 372.5 days.
record.mass_note: catalog_mass_kg is the value printed in the NSSDC catalog; the catalog does not say whether it is dry, launch or payload mass, and its meaning differs between missions.
